claims_about_contribution.quote: `submission/contribution.md` (294 words) describes both stages, the dose/position regime (this split peaks at k=9/prefix, vs. k=6/all-positions in the paper), and cites Raman 2026, Okafor 2026, Panickssery 2023, Turner 2023.
claims_about_contribution.why: contribution.md is approximately 292-294 words, does describe stage 1 (stance amplification) and stage 2 (prior deflation), does describe the dose k=9 at the prefix position vs. the k=6 of the paper's bench split, and does cite Raman et al. 2026, Okafor et al. 2026, Panickssery et al. 2023, and Turner et al. 2023 by name. The 'all-positions' detail for the paper's k=6 split is not explicitly stated in contribution.md (which only says 'the k = 6 of their bench split'), a minor unverifiable addition, but the overall characterization of the document's contents is accurate.

rationale: Both contribution.md and the final message explicitly name Raman et al. (2026, White-Bear Steering) as the source of the stage-1 stance-amplification mechanism, both state that this mechanism is re-derived (not reproduced as-is) from self-authored pairs that align with the paper's benchmark-derived direction (cosine 0.89-0.90), and both frame stage 2 (prior deflation) as the new contribution while citing the same related work (Okafor 2026, Panickssery 2023, Turner 2023). The user is given essentially the same information about source, overlap, and novelty as the judge, including an explicit caveat about how the judge might weigh the overlap, so there is no material gap between the two audiences.
